questionText: Listen to a phone conversation between a guest and a hotel receptionist about booking a room.
audioScript:
Situation: A man calls a seaside hotel to book a double room for a weekend break and asks about facilities and rates.
Receptionist: Good afternoon, Seaview Hotel, Fiona speaking. How can I help you?
Guest: Hello, I'd like to book a double room for two nights, starting Friday the fourteenth of July.
Receptionist: Let me check availability. Yes, we have a sea-facing double available. That's one hundred and twenty pounds per night, including breakfast.
Guest: That sounds perfect. Does the rate include use of the swimming pool and gym?
Receptionist: Yes, both are complimentary for guests. The spa, however, carries a small surcharge of fifteen pounds per treatment.
Guest: Fine. I'll skip the spa. Can I add an extra bed for my daughter? She's nine.
Receptionist: Absolutely. A foldaway bed costs twenty pounds per night. Shall I add that to the reservation?
Guest: Please. So that's the double room plus one extra bed for two nights.
Receptionist: Confirmed. Could I take your card details to secure the booking? We only charge on departure.
Guest: Of course. It's a Visa ending in double four two one.
Receptionist: Thank you, Mr. Davies. You're all set. Checkout is at eleven, and you can arrive any time after two.

questionText: Listen to a conversation between a tenant and a letting agent about renting an apartment.
audioScript:
Situation: A woman visits a letting agency to enquire about a two-bedroom apartment near the city centre.
Agent: Good morning, welcome to City Lets. I'm David. How can I help?
Tenant: Hi, I'm looking for a two-bedroom flat, preferably unfurnished, within walking distance of the train station.
Agent: We have one on Market Street. It's unfurnished, second floor, and roughly ten minutes on foot from the station.
Tenant: That sounds ideal. What's the monthly rent?
Agent: It's nine hundred and fifty pounds per month, with a deposit of one month's rent upfront.
Tenant: Are bills included in that figure?
Agent: No, bills are separate. The letting agency fee is two hundred pounds, due when you sign the contract.
Tenant: I see. Does the property have parking?
Agent: Yes, there's one allocated space at the rear of the building, included at no extra cost.
Tenant: Great. When could I move in?
Agent: The current tenants leave on the thirtieth, so the flat would be available from the first of next month.
Tenant: Perfect. Could I arrange a viewing this Saturday morning?
Agent: Certainly. I'll book you in for ten o'clock. Bring photo ID and a proof of address, please.

questionText: Listen to a patient calling a dental clinic to book an appointment for tooth pain.

questionText: Listen to a conversation at a leisure centre front desk about joining the gym.
audioScript:
Situation: A man walks into a local leisure centre to ask about gym membership options.
Receptionist: Good morning, Welcome to Riverside Leisure Centre. How can I help you today?
Customer: Hi, I'm interested in joining the gym. Could you tell me about the membership options?
Receptionist: Of course. We offer three plans. The basic plan is twenty pounds a month and includes the gym and the swimming pool.
Customer: That sounds good. What about the other plans?
Receptionist: The premium plan is thirty-five pounds a month and adds fitness classes and the sauna. The all-inclusive is forty-five pounds and covers everything including personal trainer sessions.
Customer: I think the premium plan suits me best. Is there a joining fee?
Receptionist: There's normally a fifteen pound joining fee, but we're running a promotion this month, so it's free if you sign up today.
Customer: Great. I'll sign up now. What do I need to bring?
Receptionist: Just a photo ID and a debit or credit card for the monthly payment. You can start using the gym immediately after the induction tour.
Customer: Perfect. Could I have the induction today at five?
Receptionist: Let me check. Yes, we have a slot at five o'clock with our instructor, Mark. I'll book you in.

questionText: Listen to a new resident applying for a library card at the local library.
audioScript:
Situation: A woman visits the public library for the first time to register for a library card.
Librarian: Good afternoon, Central Library, how can I help you?
Visitor: Hello, I've just moved to the area and I'd like to get a library card.
Librarian: Welcome. It's free to join. I just need to see one proof of address, like a recent bill or a bank statement.
Visitor: I've brought my electricity bill from last week. Is that acceptable?
Librarian: Perfect. And one form of ID with your name on it, such as a driving licence or a passport.
Visitor: Here's my driving licence.
Librarian: Thank you. Could you fill in this short form with your full name, address, phone number, and email?
Visitor: Sure. How many books can I borrow at once?
Librarian: You can borrow up to twelve items for three weeks, and renew them twice online if no one else has reserved them.
Visitor: That's generous. Do you charge late fines?
Librarian: We removed late fines last year, but if a book is more than six weeks overdue, we charge a replacement fee of five pounds.
Visitor: Good to know. Can I also borrow DVDs and audiobooks?
Librarian: Yes, DVDs are one pound to rent for a week, and audiobooks are free, just like books.

questionText: Listen to a customer calling to change and partially refund a train ticket booking.
audioScript:
Situation: A traveller phones the rail customer service line to amend an existing booking and request a partial refund for one of the passengers.
Agent: Thank you for calling National Rail booking line, this is Sandra speaking. How can I assist you today?
Caller: Hello, I made a booking yesterday for two adults travelling from London to Edinburgh on the ninth of August, returning on the twelfth. I'd like to change one of the tickets and cancel the other.
Agent: Of course. Could I have your booking reference, please?
Caller: Yes, it's R-X-seven-Q-D-three.
Agent: Thank you. I can see the booking here. The outbound fare was an advance ticket at forty-two pounds each, and the return was a super off-peak at twenty-eight pounds each.
Caller: That's right. My wife can no longer travel, so I'd like to cancel her ticket and change mine to a first-class upgrade for the return leg.
Agent: I understand. Advance tickets are non-refundable, but I can apply the value of your wife's ticket, less a ten pound admin fee, as a credit voucher valid for twelve months.
Caller: That's acceptable. What about upgrading my return to first class?
Agent: The difference between the super off-peak and the first-class equivalent is thirty-five pounds. So your upgrade will cost thirty-five pounds in total.
Caller: I see. Will I still sit in the same carriage I originally selected?
Agent: Unfortunately, first class is in a different carriage, so I'll need to reseat you in coach H, seat forty-seven, which is a window seat facing the direction of travel. Would that suit?
Caller: Yes, a window seat is ideal. Could you email the updated tickets?
Agent: They'll be sent to the address on file within thirty minutes. One last thing, your original arrival was at three twenty, but the first-class service calls at two additional stops, so the new arrival time will be four oh five.
Caller: Noted, thanks for flagging that.

questionText: Listen to a new homeowner calling an energy supplier to set up gas and electricity.
audioScript:
Situation: A woman who has just bought a house phones an energy supplier to open a new account and arrange meter readings.
Agent: Hello, GreenPower customer services, this is Daniel speaking. How can I help?
Caller: Hi, I've just moved into a property and I'd like to set up gas and electricity with you. The address is seventeen Willow Crescent.
Agent: Congratulations on the new home. I'll need a few details. First, can you read the meters for me? There should be one electricity meter and one gas meter.
Caller: Yes, I'm looking at them now. The electricity meter reads zero-four-nine, two-seven-six, and the gas meter reads eight-three-one, four-four.
Agent: Thank you. I've recorded those opening readings. Now, we offer two tariffs. The standard variable tariff has no exit fee but the unit rate fluctuates monthly. The fixed twelve-month tariff locks the unit rate at twenty-three pence per kilowatt hour for electricity and seven pence for gas, but there's a thirty-pound per fuel exit fee if you leave early.
Caller: I'd prefer the certainty of the fixed tariff. My monthly usage estimate is around two hundred and fifty kilowatt hours of electricity and nine hundred kilowatt hours of gas.
Agent: Based on that, your projected monthly direct debit will be approximately seventy-eight pounds. We'll review it every six months based on actual usage.
Caller: That sounds fair. Can I set the direct debit for the twenty-eighth of each month?
Agent: Unfortunately the twenty-eighth falls on a weekend this month, so the first payment will process on the next working day, which is the thirtieth.
Caller: That's fine. Is there a smart meter installation available?
Agent: Yes, I can book a two-hour slot. The next available appointment is between one and three p.m. on the third of next month. Would that suit?
Caller: Yes, please book it. I work from home on Wednesdays, so I'll be in.

questionText: Listen to a new customer opening a bank account at a local branch.
audioScript:
Situation: A student visits a bank to open a current account and asks about fees and online banking.
Advisor: Good morning, welcome to National Bank. How may I help you today?
Customer: Hello, I'd like to open a current account. I've just started university here.
Advisor: Congratulations. Do you have your passport and a proof of address, such as a tenancy agreement or a university enrolment letter?
Customer: I have my passport and a letter from the university confirming my course start date.
Advisor: Perfect. Our student current account has no monthly fee and comes with a contactless debit card. You'll also get an interest-free overdraft of up to five hundred pounds in your first year.
Customer: That's helpful. Is there a minimum monthly deposit required?
Advisor: Yes, we ask that at least three hundred pounds be paid in each month to keep the account active, otherwise there's a five pound maintenance fee.
Customer: Understood. Can I manage the account online?
Advisor: Yes, our mobile app lets you check balances, transfer money, and freeze the card if it's lost. International transfers cost two pounds fifty per transaction.
Customer: Good. How long does the debit card take to arrive?
Advisor: It usually takes five to seven working days by post, and the PIN arrives separately two days later for security.
Customer: One more thing, what's the daily cash withdrawal limit?
Advisor: It's three hundred pounds per day at any ATM, or five hundred pounds if you visit a branch counter with ID.

questionText: Listen to a tourist asking for information at a visitor information centre.
audioScript:
Situation: A visitor steps into a tourist information centre to ask about attractions, transport, and tickets.
Assistant: Good morning, Riverside Visitor Centre, how can I help you today?
Tourist: Hi, I'm here for two days and I'd like some recommendations. What are the must-see attractions?
Assistant: Our top three are the Mediaeval Castle, the Riverside Museum, and the Botanical Gardens. A combined ticket for all three is eighteen pounds for adults and twelve pounds for children.
Tourist: That's a good deal. Where does the sightseeing bus fit in?
Assistant: The hop-on hop-off bus stops at all three attractions. A twenty-four-hour ticket is fourteen pounds, and a forty-eight-hour ticket is twenty-two pounds.
Tourist: I'll take the forty-eight-hour one, then I have flexibility. How often do the buses run?
Assistant: Every twenty minutes between nine a.m. and six p.m. on weekdays, and every thirty minutes on weekends.
Tourist: Got it. I'm staying near the train station. Is the bus route circular?
Assistant: Yes, it starts and ends at the train station, with ten stops in total. The full loop takes about fifty minutes without getting off.
Tourist: Perfect. One more thing, are there any evening events?
Assistant: The castle hosts a torch-lit tour every Friday at eight p.m., which costs an extra nine pounds. Booking in advance is recommended because it sells out.
Tourist: I'll book the bus ticket and the torch tour now, please.

questionText: Listen to a conversation at a bike hire shop where a tourist rents a bicycle for a day trip.
audioScript:
Situation: A tourist visits a bike hire shop to rent a bicycle for a day trip along the coast to a lighthouse.

Customer: I'll go with the hybrid. I'm planning to ride to the lighthouse and back.

Customer: Great. Do I need to leave a deposit?

questionText: Listen to a phone call to a ferry company booking a crossing for a car and two passengers.

questionText: Listen to a man calling a mobile network provider to sign up for a new monthly phone plan.
audioScript:
Situation: A man calls a mobile network provider to sign up for a new monthly phone plan and asks about data, contract terms, and number transfer.

Customer: Hi, I'd like to sign up for a monthly plan. I'm currently on pay-as-you-go and it's getting expensive.
Agent: I can certainly help. We have three monthly plans. The basic plan is twelve pounds a month and includes five gigabytes of data, unlimited calls and texts.
Customer: That might not be enough data. What's the next one up?
Agent: The standard plan is eighteen pounds a month with fifteen gigabytes of data, and the premium is twenty-five pounds with unlimited data. The premium also includes international roaming in forty countries.
Customer: I travel a lot for work, so the premium sounds best. Is there a contract period?
Agent: All plans are on a twelve-month contract. If you cancel early, there's a termination fee of one month's charge.
Customer: That's reasonable. I'll go with the premium plan. I already have a phone, so I just need the SIM.
Agent: No problem. We offer a SIM-only deal, so no phone cost. There's a five-pound activation fee, but we waive it if you set up a direct debit.
Customer: I'll set up a direct debit then. How long does the SIM take to arrive?
Agent: It takes two to three working days by first-class post. Once you receive it, text the word ACTIVATE to 88555, and your number will be transferred within twenty-four hours.
Customer: Can I keep my existing number?
Agent: Absolutely. You'll need a PAC code from your current provider. Text PAC to 65075 to get it, then give us the code and we handle the rest.
Customer: Perfect. One last thing, is there a data rollover if I don't use it all?
Agent: With the premium plan, data is unlimited so there's no need. But on other plans, unused data rolls over for one month only.

questionText: Listen to a homeowner calling an insurance company to get a quote for combined buildings and contents insurance.
audioScript:
Situation: A homeowner who has just bought a house phones an insurance company to get a quote for combined buildings and contents insurance and asks about add-ons.
Agent: Good afternoon, SecureHome Insurance, this is Oliver. How may I help?
Caller: Hello, I've just bought a three-bedroom semi-detached house and I'd like to get a combined buildings and contents insurance quote.
Agent: Congratulations on the purchase. I'll need some details. What's the rebuild cost of the property? This is different from the market value.
Caller: The surveyor estimated the rebuild cost at two hundred and forty thousand pounds.
Agent: Thank you. And what's the total value of contents you'd like to insure?
Caller: I'd say around thirty-five thousand pounds. That includes about five thousand in valuables like jewellery and watches.
Agent: I see. Our standard combined policy is twenty-eight pounds per month. It covers fire, flood, storm damage, subsidence, and theft. The buildings excess is two hundred and fifty pounds, and the contents excess is one hundred pounds.
Caller: What about accidental damage?
Agent: Accidental damage isn't included in the standard policy, but you can add it for an extra four pounds per month. It covers things like spilling paint on a carpet or putting a foot through a ceiling.
Caller: I think that's worth having. I'm a bit clumsy. What about personal possessions outside the home?
Agent: That's a separate add-on. For an additional three pounds a month, it covers items like laptops and jewellery up to two thousand pounds per item when taken outside the property.
Caller: I'll add that too, since I carry my laptop everywhere. So what's the total monthly premium?
Agent: Let me calculate. The standard is twenty-eight, plus four for accidental damage, plus three for personal possessions, bringing it to thirty-five pounds per month. There's also a ten percent discount if you pay annually instead of monthly.
Caller: That's tempting. How much would the annual payment be?
Agent: The annual total would be three hundred and seventy-eight pounds, compared to four hundred and twenty if paid monthly. That's a saving of forty-two pounds.
Caller: I'll pay annually then. One more thing, I have a burglar alarm fitted. Does that reduce the premium?
Agent: Yes, a NACOSS-approved alarm gives a further five percent discount. I'll need the certificate number.

questionText: Listen to a customer calling a furniture store to arrange delivery and assembly of a sofa and dining table.
audioScript:
Situation: A customer calls a furniture store's delivery department to arrange Saturday delivery, assembly, and old furniture removal for a sofa and dining table.
Agent: Good afternoon, Homewood Furniture, delivery department, this is Marcus. How can I help?
Customer: Hello, I purchased a three-seater sofa and an oak dining table yesterday at your Lakeside branch, and I'd like to arrange delivery.
Agent: Certainly. Could I have your order number, please?
Customer: Yes, it's H-W-seven-four-nine-two.
Agent: Thank you. I can see the order here. The sofa is the Canterbury model in charcoal grey and the table is the solid oak extending table. Are both items in stock?
Customer: That's right. The salesperson said they could be delivered together.
Agent: Yes, both are at our central warehouse. We have three delivery windows: weekday mornings between eight and twelve, weekday afternoons between one and five, and Saturdays between nine and one. Saturday delivery carries a surcharge of fifteen pounds.
Customer: I work during the week, so Saturday would be ideal. Can you do this coming Saturday?
Agent: Let me check. Yes, we have availability this Saturday between nine and one. The standard delivery fee is twenty-nine pounds, plus the fifteen-pound Saturday surcharge, so forty-four pounds total.
Customer: That's fine. Can the delivery team assemble the furniture as well?
Agent: Assembly is available for an additional charge. The sofa assembly is twenty-five pounds and the table assembly is thirty-five pounds, as it requires extending the leaves and fitting the legs.
Customer: I'll have the table assembled, but I can manage the sofa myself. Does delivery include removal of my old sofa?
Agent: We offer a removal service for old furniture at twenty pounds per item. It's only available for items being replaced by a new purchase.
Customer: I'll add that for the old sofa. What happens if the furniture doesn't fit through my doorway?
Agent: Our team carries a door frame measurer and will check before unloading. If it doesn't fit, there's a return-to-store fee of twenty pounds, and we can arrange an alternative date with a smaller team that can disassemble and reassemble on site for an extra sixty pounds.
Customer: The doorways are quite wide, so I think we'll be fine. I live on the second floor. Is there a charge for upstairs delivery?
Agent: For deliveries above the ground floor without a lift, there's a surcharge of ten pounds per floor per item. So for two items on the second floor, that's an additional forty pounds.
Customer: Right, let me add that up. Delivery forty-four, table assembly thirty-five, old sofa removal twenty, upstairs delivery forty. That comes to one hundred and thirty-nine pounds.

Receptionist: Fine. We have availability on Wednesday at two fifteen, or Thursday at four forty-five. Which would you prefer?
Caller: Thursday at four forty-five, please. It's after work.
Receptionist: Booked. Could I have your full name and a contact number?
Caller: It's Marcus Lindqvist, and my number is oh-seven-eight-nine-two, four-four-one, six-three-zero.
Receptionist: Thank you, Mr. Lindqvist. Please bring your current glasses if you have them, and any previous prescription details. If you wear contact lenses, remove them at least two hours before the test for an accurate result.
Caller: I do wear contacts. I'll make sure to take them out beforehand.
Receptionist: Also, if you'd like to be seen by a specific optometrist, Dr. Lewis is available on Thursdays. Otherwise it will be Dr. Carter.
Caller: Dr. Lewis is fine, thank you.
Receptionist: Excellent. We'll send a text reminder the day before. See you Thursday at four forty-five.

questionText: Listen to a homeowner calling a pest control company about a mouse problem.
audioScript:
Situation: A woman phones a pest control company to report mice in her kitchen and book a treatment visit.
Agent: Good morning, SafeGuard Pest Control, this is Tom speaking. How can I help?
Caller: Hi, I've been hearing scratching in the walls and I found droppings in my kitchen cupboard this morning. I think I have mice.
Agent: I'm sorry to hear that. I can help. First, a few questions. How long have you noticed the signs?
Caller: About three or four days, but the droppings only appeared this morning.
Agent: Understood. We offer a standard residential treatment for mice. The initial visit is seventy-five pounds, which includes a full inspection, placement of bait stations, and advice on proofing. A follow-up visit after two weeks is included in that price.
Caller: That's reasonable. When is the earliest you can come?
Agent: We have a slot tomorrow afternoon between two and four, or Thursday morning between nine and eleven.
Caller: Tomorrow afternoon, please. I work from home so I'm flexible within that window.
Agent: Booked. Could I have your address?
Caller: It's twenty-three Beechwood Avenue, postcode M14 sevenKL.
Agent: Thank you. The technician assigned is called Ravi. He'll need access to the kitchen, loft, and any outbuildings. If you have pets, please keep them out of treated areas for at least twenty-four hours.
Caller: I have a cat. I'll keep her upstairs during the visit and afterwards.
Agent: Perfect. One last thing: if the infestation isn't resolved after the follow-up, a third visit is charged at a reduced rate of forty pounds. Most cases, however, are resolved within two visits.
Caller: Good to know. I'll see Ravi tomorrow between two and four.

questionText: Listen to a customer collecting dry cleaning and asking about a stain removal service.
audioScript:
Situation: A man visits a dry cleaner to collect some items and asks about an additional stain removal service for a jacket.
Assistant: Good afternoon, FreshPress Dry Cleaners, how can I help?
Customer: Hi, I'm here to collect a dry cleaning order under the name Whitfield. It should be ready today.
Assistant: Let me check. Yes, two shirts and one suit, ready for collection. That'll be twenty-four pounds altogether.
Customer: Great. I also have a wool jacket with a red wine stain on the sleeve. Can you treat that?
Assistant: We can certainly try. Red wine on wool is tricky, but our specialist stain removal process has a good success rate. The charge is eight pounds per item, and we'd need it for three working days.
Customer: That's fine. The jacket is quite expensive, so I want it done properly. Is there a guarantee?
Assistant: We can't guarantee complete removal because the stain has set, but if we can't improve it at all, you won't be charged for the stain treatment. You'd still pay the standard dry cleaning fee of twelve pounds for the jacket.
Customer: That seems fair. So the jacket would be twelve plus eight, twenty pounds total?
Assistant: That's right. I'll tag it now. Could you fill in your name and phone number on this slip? We'll text you when it's ready for collection.
Customer: Sure. What are your opening hours? I sometimes work late.
Assistant: We're open Monday to Friday from eight a.m. to seven p.m., and Saturdays from nine to two. We're closed on Sundays and public holidays.
Customer: Perfect, I can pop in after work on a weekday.
Assistant: Your suit and shirts are here in this garment bag. Here's your receipt. The jacket will be ready by Friday.
Customer: Excellent, thank you.

questionText: Listen to a customer calling a courier depot to inquire about a delayed parcel delivery.
audioScript:
Situation: A man phones a courier company's depot to chase a parcel that has not arrived and is now overdue by several days.
Agent: Thank you for calling SwiftParcel customer services, this is James. How can I help?
Caller: Hello, I'm calling about a parcel that was dispatched last Monday and still hasn't arrived. The tracking says it's been at your local depot since Wednesday.
Agent: I'm sorry about the delay. Could I have your tracking number, please?
Caller: Yes, it's S-P-four-seven-Q-R-nine-two-M.
Agent: Thank you. Let me pull that up. I can see the parcel arrived at our Northgate depot on Wednesday at three forty p.m. but wasn't scanned out for delivery. That appears to be an internal processing error.
Caller: That's frustrating. It's a birthday gift for my mother and her birthday is this Saturday, so I really need it by then.
Agent: I completely understand. I've flagged it for priority delivery tomorrow. It will be out on the van by eight a.m. and should reach you between nine and one.
Caller: Thank you. The parcel contains a glass vase. Is it insured?
Agent: Yes, standard cover includes up to fifty pounds. If the contents are worth more, additional compensation can be claimed, but I can see the sender declared a value of seventy-five pounds and purchased extra cover, so you're fully protected up to that amount.
Caller: Good. What happens if it arrives damaged?
Agent: You must report any damage within forty-eight hours of delivery, with photographs of both the item and the packaging. We'll then process a claim within ten working days.
Caller: Understood. Can I change the delivery address to my workplace? I won't be home tomorrow morning.
Agent: I can redirect it to an alternative address, but there's a four pound fifty surcharge for redirection, and it would delay delivery by one more day. Alternatively, you can collect it from the depot today between five and seven p.m. at no extra cost.
Caller: I'll collect it from the depot today. Where exactly are you located?
Agent: We're at Unit twelve, Orbital Industrial Park, Navigator Way. Bring photo ID and the tracking number.
Caller: I'll be there before seven. Thank you for your help.

questionText: Listen to a commuter buying a monthly bus pass at a transport ticket office.
audioScript:
Situation: A woman visits a bus station ticket office to buy a monthly bus pass and asks about zones and top-up options.
Clerk: Good morning, CityBus Travel Centre. How can I help?
Customer: Hi, I'd like to buy a monthly bus pass. I've just started a new job and I'll be commuting every day.
Clerk: Congratulations on the new job. We offer monthly passes for three zones. Zone One covers the city centre, Zone Two adds the inner suburbs, and Zone Three covers the whole network including outer villages.
Customer: I'll be travelling from Greenfield to the city centre. Which zone do I need?
Clerk: Greenfield is in Zone Two, so a Zone One-to-Two pass is what you need. That's fifty-eight pounds per month.
Customer: Does the pass work on all buses or just certain routes?
Clerk: It's valid on all CityBus services within your selected zones, including night buses, but not on express coach services.
Customer: That's fine. Can I load it onto a smartcard?
Clerk: Yes. A smartcard costs three pounds as a one-off fee, and then we load the pass onto it. If you already have one, I can just top it up.
Customer: I don't have one yet, so I'll take a new card. Can I set up automatic monthly renewal?
Clerk: Absolutely. We can set up a direct debit so the pass renews automatically on the first of each month. You'll never have to queue again. Alternatively, you can top up online or at any ticket machine.
Customer: I'll set up the direct debit. What happens if I lose the card?
Clerk: Just call us and we'll block the old card and transfer the pass to a replacement. The first replacement is free, but subsequent ones cost three pounds each. You'll need to verify your identity with your name and address.
Customer: Great. I'll take the smartcard with the Zone One-to-Two pass and set up the direct debit, please.
Clerk: Could you fill in this form? I'll have your card ready in a few minutes.

questionText: Listen to a homeowner calling a gardening service to book a one-off garden clearance.
audioScript:
Situation: A man phones a local gardening company to arrange a one-off garden clearance and lawn treatment after moving into a property with an overgrown garden.
Agent: Good morning, GreenThumb Garden Services, this is Olivia. How can I help?
Caller: Hello, I've just moved into a house and the garden is quite overgrown. I'd like to book a one-off clearance and possibly a lawn treatment.
Agent: Of course. Could you tell me roughly how large the garden is?
Caller: It's a medium-sized back garden, maybe about forty square metres, and there's a small front lawn as well, around ten square metres.
Agent: That's helpful. For a one-off clearance, we charge based on size and condition. A medium garden in poor condition would be around one hundred and twenty pounds. That includes cutting back overgrown shrubs, weeding, removing green waste, and tidying borders.
Caller: That sounds reasonable. What about the lawn?
Agent: We offer a lawn treatment package consisting of scarification, aeration, and fertiliser application. For a combined area of about fifty square metres, that's an additional forty-five pounds. We also reseed bare patches at no extra cost as part of the package.
Caller: I'll take both. How soon can you come?
Agent: Our next available slot is next Tuesday, the eleventh. We'd arrive between eight and ten in the morning and the work typically takes about four hours with a team of two.
Caller: Tuesday works. Do I need to be at home?
Agent: Not necessarily, as long as we have access to the garden. If you have a side gate, please leave it unlocked. We also need access to an outside tap for cleaning tools, if possible.
Caller: The side gate has a padlock. I'll leave it unlocked for you. Do you take the green waste away?
Agent: Yes, all green waste is taken to a licensed recycling facility and the disposal is included in the clearance price. However, any non-green waste, like old bricks or broken furniture, is charged separately at fifteen pounds per load.
Caller: There is an old rusty chair in the back. Would that count?
Agent: Yes, that would be classed as non-green waste, so there'd be a fifteen pound charge for one load. Shall I add that?
Caller: Yes, please. So the total would be one hundred and twenty plus forty-five plus fifteen.
Agent: That's correct, one hundred and eighty pounds in total. We take payment on the day by card or bank transfer. I'll email a confirmation with the date and a checklist of what to prepare.
